- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes in sentiment or price, particularly in the 10–15 day horizon.  
- Model tends to overreact to recent price volatility; smooth out sharp peaks and troughs in forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is above 80–85% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days prior, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is consistently negative; cap forecast at 75–80% of 30-day moving average.
